voyage.name: MegaPass Istanbul
voyage.content: MegaPass Istanbul offers several city pass options combining Bosphorus cruises, guided tours, and access to key attractions. Travelers can choose from: Classic City Pass: Includes a Bosphorus cruise, guided Blue Mosque tour, transportation card with 5 rides, and access to two attractions. Premium City Pass: Adds a hop-on hop-off bus tour, a Turkish bath experience, and access to four attractions. Deluxe City Pass: In

voyage.name: Sultanahmet Mosque
voyage.content: The defining image of Istanbul, dominating the skyline with its great dome and six minarets. Completed in 1617 for Sultan Ahmed I, it's still a working mosque, so dress appropriately and avoid prayer times. Enter via the courtyard on the SW side. You step (shoeless) into the blue-tiled prayer hall beneath the main dome and its semi-domes. The mihrab is of finely carved marble, well-lit, and the minbar (pulpit) next t

voyage.name: Hagia Sophia
voyage.content: The third and grandest of the churches on this site, completed in 537 AD. The 30-m diameter dome covers what was for over 1000 years the largest enclosed space in the world, only surpassed in 1520 by Seville cathedral. It used "pendentive" architecture to throw the dome's weight onto four stout pillars, a design that inspired many Eastern Orthodox churches and Ottoman mosques. It became a mosque after the Ottoman con

voyage.name: Topkapı Palace
voyage.price: Adult 2750 TL (combi for Palace, Harem and Hagia Irene)
voyage.content: The imperial enclave of the Ottoman emperors for four centuries. Lavishly decorated, with exhibitions of fine craftmanship and four courts of increasing grandeur. The second court has the Harem and the State Treasury, housing a weaponry display. On the right, towards the Bosphorus, there is the kitchen exhibition, also with a collection of coffee cups throughout the centuries. The third court has the Imperial Treasur

voyage.name: Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum
voyage.content: A profusion of carpets, rugs, calligraphy, pottery, Qu'rans and other manuscripts. The museum is housed in the Palace of Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (1495–1536), who was grand vizier to Suleiman the Magnificent, and the best of pals till Suleiman had him murdered.

voyage.name: Basilica Cistern
voyage.content: Vast underground cistern built by Justinian in 532 to store the city's water, the largest and best-known of the hundreds constructed. It's a cathedral-like space with 336 richly decorated columns. Time was you explored in a little rowing boat, but tourist numbers have soared and water levels have dropped, so now you follow a boardwalk, with lights, piped music and art installations. It's sometimes a film location, an

voyage.name: Museum of Archaeology
voyage.price: Adult €15. Beware of the ticket office staff adding the audio guide to the ticket price without asking if you want it. It's not compulsory and you don't need it. Check the bill before paying!
voyage.hours: Daily 09:00-17:30. The Tiled Kiosk and the Museum of Oriental Art are closed as of October 2025
voyage.content: Turkey was slow to protect its antiquities and to display them properly, but in 1867 Sultan Abdülaziz toured the museums of Paris, London and Vienna and saw what was needed. The main collection is in a grand neo-classical building of 1891, with two annexes for ancient art and Islamic art. Exhibits include Sumerian tablets, pieces of the wall of Babylon, Roman statues, and the Alexander Sarcophagus. There are very det

voyage.name: Museum of the History of Science and Technology in Islam
voyage.alt: İslam Bilim ve Teknoloji Tarihi Müzesi
voyage.content: Museum in a restored building that was the stables for Topkapı Palace. It exhibits various instruments for astronomy, clocks, pumps, weaponry, a steam-powered döner spit, and so on developed in Islamic realms down the centuries, but these are modern repro, and explanations of their context are skimpy. Islamic science and technology preceded that of Europe, as they insist, but they get the tone wrong, as if that was t

voyage.name: Istanbul Railway Museum
voyage.content: Housed in the Europe-side railway terminus of 1890, this exhibits Ottoman and modern Turkish railway history. The Orient Express came and went from here, with passengers for further east transferring to ferries then the Asia-side terminus of Haydarpaşa, for trains to Crimea, Baghdad and Damascus.

voyage.name: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
voyage.content: Built in 1564 by Mimar Sinan for Rüstem Pasha, Grand Vizier of Suleiman the Magnificent, this small mosque has an interior covered by beautiful Iznik pottery, then at its zenith.

voyage.name: Beyazit II Mosque
voyage.content: Imposing mosque built 1500/05. The other parts of the religious complex have found secular use.

voyage.name: Great Palace Mosaics Museum
voyage.content: This museum hosts the pavement mosaics of the Great Palace of Constantinople, which stretched from the Hippodrome to the coast.

voyage.name: Sokollu Mehmet Pasha Mosque
voyage.content: Sokollu Mehmet Pasha was the grand vizier and de facto ruler of the Ottoman Empire during its 16th century golden age. He commissioned this mosque, one of three in the city to bear his name, but the sloping site was a challenge. He hired the best, Mimar Sinan, who completed it in 979 AH / 1571 AD, with the slope resolved by a fronting courtyard above shops and a medrese. The interior has outstanding İznik blue tiles,

voyage.name: Little Hagia Sophia
voyage.content: Built as the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus around 530 AD, the same time as Hagia Sophia, but their styles differ. Transformed into a mosque in the early 1500s, it's beautifully decorated, with fine marble details, and has a pleasanter atmosphere than the larger busy mosques. The adjoining madrasa houses craft shops.

voyage.name: Theodosius Cistern
voyage.content: This was rediscovered in 2010 when an overlying building was demolished. It was built circa 430 AD to store water brought in by Valens Aqueduct. It's smaller than the better-known Basilica Cistern, but better lit, more atmospheric and less touristy.

voyage.name: Nuruosmaniye Mosque
voyage.content: Built 1748-55, this launched the style we call Ottoman Baroque, with its grand central dome and pencil-thin minarets. It was copied throughout their empire and is replicated in new mosques even today. The name means "light of the Ottomans," and the interior uses light powdery decor, bathed with much more natural light than its gloomier classical predecessors. The complex also has a madrasa and the imaret (public soup

voyage.name: Molla Zeyrek Mosque
voyage.content: This is a triple structure: the church of the Monastery of Pantokrator built 1118, then a public church circa 1136 plus a chapel that served as a royal mausoleum. It became a mosque and medresse in Ottoman times, but without massive alteration so it's a prime example of middle-Byzantine architecture. It's nowadays again a mosque, photogenic by day or dusk but the area should be avoided at night.

voyage.name: Kalenderhane Mosque
voyage.content: Built circa 1200 as the Eastern Orthodox Theotokos Kyriotissa Church, after the Ottoman conquest it was handed over to the Qalandari, a Sufi sect. In the mid-18th century it was converted to a Sunni mosque, and its mosaics were plastered over. The original appearance was restored in the 1970s.

voyage.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
voyage.content: On top of a hill overlooking the Golden Horn, this is a magnificent mosque built by Sinan in the 1550s. It was centrepiece of a large külliye, a religious complex which included madrasas, a public kitchen and a hospital.. The small cemetery east has the mausoleums of Suleiman the Magnificent and of his wife Hurrem Sultan or Roxelana.

voyage.name: Fatih Mosque
voyage.content: The original mosque was built between 1463-1470 by the Greek architect Atik Sinan, by order of Sultan Mehmet II the Conqueror, on the site of the former Church of the Holy Apostles, which had served as Byzantine Imperial burial place for a thousand years. The grand complex with eight medreses, a library, hospital, hospice, caravanserai, market, hamam, primary school and public soup kitchen was smashed again and again

voyage.name: Hırka-i Şerif Mosque
voyage.content: Completed in 1851, this houses a mantle said to have been worn by the prophet Muhammad. The mantle is displayed during Ramadan.

voyage.name: St George's Cathedral
voyage.alt: Turkish: Aya Yorgi, Greek: Agíou Geōrgíou
voyage.content: This is modest from the outside, as the Ottomans would not permit non-Muslim religious buildings to rival the mosques. The interior is lavish but its chief importance is as the senior Eastern Orthodox church. Their Patriarchate has been housed here since 1586 when they were ejected from Agia Sophia.

voyage.name: Phanar Greek Orthodox College
voyage.alt: Turkish: Özel Fener Rum Lisesi, Greek: Μεγάλη του Γένους Σχολή
voyage.content: This is the red-brick castle seen south of St George. Built 1881/83, it teaches the standard Turkish curriculum plus Greek language and culture, and the tower houses an observatory. No visits.

voyage.name: Fethiye Mosque
voyage.content: The Church of Theotokos Pammakaristos ("All-Blessed Mother of God") was built between the 11th and 12th centuries. The parekklesion or side-chapel was added maybe 1300, with rich mosaics. The main building became a mosque in 1591, named for Sultan Murad III's conquest (fetih, hence Fethiye) of Georgia and Azerbaijan: the interior was opened up, but the chapel was undisturbed and in modern times became a museum. In 20

voyage.name: St Stephen Church
voyage.content: A remarkable Bulgarian Orthodox church better known as Demir Kilise, "Iron Church", as it's a cast iron prefab. The Bulgarians split from the Greek Orthodox and established their own wooden church in 1870, which burned down. The ground was too weak for a masonry or concrete structure so they opted for cast iron. The sections were cast in Vienna, shipped here and assembled, to open in 1898. The church was renovated in

voyage.name: Ahrida Synagogue
voyage.content: This was built in the 1430s by Grecian Jews ("Romaniotes") from the city of Ohrid, now in North Macedonia. The district of Balat was a Jewish quarter, swelled from 1492 by those expelled from Spain. The synagogue is only open for pre-arranged tours.

voyage.name: Palace of the Porphyrogenitus
voyage.content: The Byzantines built several great palaces in Constantinople and this is the only one to survive almost intact. It's from the late 13th century, in typical alternating marble and red-brick rows, and was an imperial residence: Porphyrogenitus means "born to the purple" indicating the heir to the crown. Yet it was merely an annex or pavilion within the much greater Palace of Blachernae, of which nothing else remains. I

voyage.name: Kariye Mosque
voyage.price: Free for Turkish citizens, 20€ for everyone else
voyage.content: Chora means countryside, and when built as a monastery in the 4th century it stood outside the Constantine walls; a century later, it was incorporated into the Theodosian walls. It was rebuilt in the 11th century then wrecked by an earthquake, so the structure and fabulous mosaics you see now are from the 14th century. When the church was converted to a mosque in 1500 the mosaics were plastered over, and only restore

voyage.name: Panorama 1453 History Museum
voyage.content: This is a circular indoor space enclosed by a 3D depiction of the Ottomans breaching the Walls of Constantinople on 29 May 1453, with sound effects. It's over-priced, unhistorical and tourist-trappy.

voyage.name: Koca Mustafa Pasha Mosque
voyage.content: Built in the early 5th century as a monastery dedicated to Saint Andrew the Apostle, in 766 it was the burial place of Saint Andrew of Crete and was later re-dedicated to him. It was rebuilt in the late 9th century and again in the 13th, then around 1490 converted into a mosque. From the 16th century it was occupied by the Dervishes, when the legend arose that a chain hung to a cypress tree in the courtyard was a tru

voyage.name: Monastery of Stoudios
voyage.content: Byzantine monastery complex built in 463 AD. In the 15th century it served as İmrahor Mosque, but was wrecked by fires and earthquakes. A ruin it remains, and plans to restore it as a mosque have come to nothing. You'll probably find it locked.

voyage.name: Yedikule Fortress
voyage.content: The Golden Gate was the ceremonial entrance through the Theodosian city walls. After the Ottomans captured the city in 1453, Mehmed II needed a stronghold for his treasures and documents. The gate was therefore bricked up and the walls reinforced into a fortress, with valuables stored in its seven towers, hence yedi kule. In the following century the treasury moved to Topkapi Palace and the fort became a prison for h

voyage.name: Balat
voyage.content: A neighborhood with colorful houses and stairs all along.

voyage.name: Hürrem Sultan Hamamı
voyage.content: Bathhouse built in 1556 by Mimar Sinan, the chief Ottoman architect, at the request of Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana), wife of Suleiman the Magnificent. It was built over the former public baths of Zeuxippus, abandoned around 713. Restored in 2011, it's now an upmarket spa.

voyage.name: Çemberlitaş Hamamı
voyage.content: Built in 1584, credited to Mimar Sinan but he probably only had light-touch supervision. It was astride the city's highway from Europe and very profitable, in spite of multiple earthquakes and fires. It fell out of use late 19th century but in the 21st was revived as a tourist experience.

voyage.name: Cağaloğlu Hamamı
voyage.content: Built in 1741, the last major hamam opened in the Ottoman era. It has ornate architecture, great service and a stellar cast of famous visitors. Prices to match, and only tourists now use it.

voyage.name: Şifa Hamamı
voyage.content: Established in 1777, this is one of the cheaper options. It's marble throughout and the fittings could be original. It has a mixed main section and a separate female section for the scrubbing.

voyage.name: Süleymaniye Hamamı
voyage.content: Commissioned by Süleyman the Magnificent and built by Mimar Sinan in 1550, at the east edge of Süleymaniye mosque complex. It had private cubicles for distinguished visitors such as the sultan, but was mostly a standard working-class bathhouse. It was restored in 2001 and is nowadays touristy. It's the only mixed hamam in Istanbul, but mixed sessions are only for couples and families.

voyage.name: Grand Bazaar
voyage.content: Vast historic covered bazaar with over 4400 shops. These are organized around their wares, so the silver jewellers are clustered together, shoe shops are together in another alley, and so on. Prices are double those elsewhere and locals don't shop here, but it's an atmospheric place with a vast selection, and some of the antique dealers have genuinely rare stock.

voyage.name: Egyptian Bazaar
voyage.content: Smaller than Grand Bazaar, it specialises in herbs and spices. Very touristy, but prices (even after haggling) are twice those in the rest of the city.

voyage.name: Mehmet Cetinkaya Gallery
voyage.content: Attractive but pricey textiles.

voyage.name: Ilmek Antika Carpet & Textile
voyage.content: Sells rugs and kilims as well as pillowcases (all produced in Uzbekistan). Pillowcases are between €10 and 60, depending on the material.

voyage.name: Kalsedon
voyage.content: Raw gems and finished jewellery, especially chalcedony, the semi-precious stone named for the ancient town of Chalcedon, nowadays Kadıköy across the Bosphorus.

voyage.name: Historia AVM
voyage.content: AVM (alışveriş merkezi) means a shopping mall, and Historia is the only one in the Old City. Usual selections of garments, electronics, furniture, a large supermarket, plus a bowling alley, fast food and a cinema. Across the alley, Fenari İsa Mosque was an early Byzantine church, renovated as a mosque in the 1970s.

voyage.name: Osman Gourmet Restaurant
voyage.content: Inexpensive family-friendly restaurant.

voyage.name: Karadeniz Aile Pide ve Kebap Salonu
voyage.content: Their specialty is pide.

voyage.name: Meşhur Pideci Orhan Usta
voyage.content: Welcoming small restaurant, good value.

voyage.name: Pak Pide Pizza Salonu
voyage.content: Relaxing place for traditional pide.

voyage.name: Ali Usta Çiğ Köfte
voyage.content: Good value Çiǧ köfte (spicy wrap with a vegan tatar) takeaway. Ali the owner is an Instagram celeb for his videos jibing customers, so you may be in a long line.

voyage.name: Efsane Kahvaltı
voyage.content: Great place for breakfast in a non-touristy area.

voyage.name: Buyruk Esnaf Lokantası
voyage.content: A place that serves home-made style foods ("ev yemekleri") which you can order from the counter. Great variety.

voyage.name: Doy Doy Restaurant
voyage.content: Cafe spread over three floors and a roof terrace with views over the sea and Blue Mosque. Good range of Turkish meals and mezes, with veggie choices.

voyage.name: Palatium Cafe & Restaurant
voyage.content: Decent trad food and ice cold beer. Lounge in the comfy bean-bag chairs, and backgammon and Nargileh are available. The restaurant looks down into the foundations of a Roman-era palace.

voyage.name: Cafe Amedros
voyage.content: Good Ottoman cuisine with veggie and GF choices.

voyage.name: Rumeli Restaurant
voyage.content: Not cheap, but good value for its Ottoman and Turkish cuisine, service and vibe.

voyage.name: Korecan
voyage.content: Good Korean cuisine.

voyage.name: Virginia Angus Steakhouse
voyage.content: Steaks, burgers and similar.

voyage.name: Burgerillas
voyage.content: Decent burgers, sit in or take away. They have ten other city locations.

voyage.name: Changcheng
voyage.content: Good Chinese food.

voyage.name: Olden 1772
voyage.content: A trip in both history and gastronomy.

voyage.name: Sarayburnu Aile Çay Bahçesi
voyage.content: Open-air cafe on the coast with great views, though the park is grubby. Tea, coffee and many flavours of hubble-bubble.

voyage.name: Anadolu Nargile
voyage.content: Shisha / hookah cafe in the courtyard of the former Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medrese, so plenty of Ottoman ambience.

voyage.name: Vefa Bozacısı
voyage.content: Established in 1876, this cafe specializes in boza, a ferment of bulgur wheat with a sweetish tart taste. A favourite of the Ottomans, it's still popular in the Balkans and Central Asia. It's less than 1% alcohol, but it was the closest you got to being off your head in Neolithic times.

voyage.name: Blue Tuana Hotel
voyage.content: Very small rooms.

voyage.name: Star Holiday Hotel
voyage.content: Friendly hotel, rooms have air-con, TV and minibar.

voyage.name: Deniz Houses Hotel
voyage.content: Rooms with own bathroom, cable TV, air-con.

voyage.name: Istanbul Holiday Hotel
voyage.content: Clean rooms with en suite bathroom and satellite TV.

voyage.name: Elasophia Hotel
voyage.alt: formerly Dongyang; 100 m west of Agia Sophia
voyage.content: Rooms with en suite bathroom, satellite TV, and internet access.

voyage.name: Stone Hotel Istanbul
voyage.content: Simple rooms with en-suite bathroom and satellite TV. Variable on cleanliness.

voyage.name: Hotel Alp Guesthouse
voyage.content: Clean friendly place, all rooms en-suite.

voyage.name: Grand Anka Hotel
voyage.content: Modern rooms, good location and usually clean.

voyage.name: Tulip Guesthouse
voyage.price: Dorm 1000 TL ppn, double room 3000 TL
voyage.content: Welcoming and helpful staff, solo women feel safe.

voyage.name: Avrasya Hostel
voyage.content: Amazing value for the location, with six and eight bed dorms, helpful and friendly staff. No real common room.

voyage.name: Yeni Otel
voyage.content: Basic but central, clean and friendly.

voyage.name: Nomade Old City Hotel
voyage.content: Neat cozy hotel near the main sights. They have another on Akbıyık Cd..

voyage.name: Tulip House
voyage.content: Small mid-range hotel, clean and central but needs a lot of maintenance. Try to get a south-facing room with balcony.

voyage.name: Sarnıç Hotel
voyage.content: Central and clean, some noise, good value for the price. Many stairs, not suitable for the disabled.

voyage.name: Hotel Armagrandi Spina
voyage.content: Small friendly hotel.

voyage.name: Armada Hotel
voyage.content: Clean comfy place near the seafront. Rooftop restaurant has views of the sea and the Blue Mosque.

voyage.name: Sultanhan Hotel
voyage.content: Welcoming five-floor hotel with Ottoman-style décor, next to Theodosius Cistern.

voyage.name: Blue House Rooftop
voyage.content: Very central comfy 3-star.

voyage.name: Empress Zoe
voyage.content: Pleasant hotel in a quiet street near Agia Sophia, with simple rooms decorated in Turkish style.

voyage.name: Esans Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel on a quiet street 3 minutes walk from Agia Sofya, decorated in Ottoman style. The rooftop terrace looks out over the Sea of Marmara and Princes Islands.

voyage.name: Ibrahim Pasha
voyage.content: Pleasant small hotel 100 m west of Blue Mosque.

voyage.name: Dersaadet Hotel
voyage.content: Decorated in 19th century Ottoman-style, with great welcome and service.

voyage.name: Hotel Niles
voyage.content: Comfy place near the Grand Bazaar.

voyage.name: Hotel Inter Istanbul
voyage.content: In a quiet area with modern rooms.

voyage.name: Erguvan Hotel
voyage.content: Value-for-money hotel near seafront.

voyage.name: Garden House Istanbul
voyage.content: Small well-furnished rooms around a garden courtyard.

voyage.name: Hotel Tashkonak
voyage.content: Small rooms but friendly staff and sea views.

voyage.name: Hotel Sultan Hill
voyage.content: Rebuild of an 18th century Ottoman mansion. There are 17 rooms, a traditional courtyard and a roof terrace bar with panoramic views.

voyage.name: Yigitalp
voyage.content: Boxy inexpensive place often used by tour groups.

voyage.name: Hotel Sultania
voyage.content: Charming hotel with 42 rooms, each dedicated to a wife of the sultan.

voyage.name: Sirkeci Mansion Hotel
voyage.content: Charming friendly hotel near Sirkeci station.

voyage.name: Four Seasons at Sultanahmet
voyage.content: A converted prison built in 1918 near Sultanahmet mosque, great reviews for comfort and service. Their sister hotel is further up the Bosphorus.

voyage.name: Wyndham Old City Hotel
voyage.content: 87 rooms with spa and pool. Dreadful reviews in late 2024 but they've since much improved.

voyage.name: Doubletree by Hilton Old Town
voyage.content: Clean welcoming modern hotel.

voyage.name: Galata Tower
voyage.content: It was built by the Genoese in the 14th century on the city walls of Galata, marking the highest point of their territory. Ride an elevator and take two flights of stairs to the top, then walk the parapet for a 360°-view of Istanbul, including the entire Sultanahmet peninsula: crowned by Topkapı Palace, the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia. A beautiful spot worthy of a lot of pictures.

voyage.name: Galata Convent of Whirling Dervishes
voyage.content: A ritual dancing hall of the mystical Mevlevi order, the followers of the teachings of Mewlānā Rumi. The quiet and peaceful garden is a welcome escape from the hustle and bustle of Beyoğlu. The oldest Mevlevi lodge in Istanbul, the convent was started in 1491, when the surrounding area was, hard to believe today but, pure wilderness beyond the city walls of Galata, although the current building dates back to 1855, as

voyage.name: Kasimpaşa Mevlevihanesi
voyage.content: a Mevlevi cultural center opened in 2024 which regularly offers Dervish sema ceremonies. There are also some posters with information in Turkish about the Mevlevi movement and a gift shop, but not much else to be seen.

voyage.name: Crimean Memorial Church
voyage.price: Free but 10 TL donation is requested for maintenance of the church
voyage.content: A neo-gothic Anglican cathedral which would not be out of place in northwestern Europe, the Crimean Memorial Church was built for the Protestant community of the city by Britain in the late 19th century. It was named in honour of the soldiers died in the Crimean War of 1856, fought against Russia by the allied Ottoman and British Empires. The congregation of the church today mostly consists of Anglican East Asians an

voyage.name: Arap Camii
voyage.alt: Galata Camii, San Paolo, San Domenico
voyage.content: The building was erected as a Roman Catholic church in 1325 by the friars of the Dominican Order, near or above an earlier chapel dedicated to Saint Paul (Italian: San Paolo) in 1233. In 1299, the Dominican Friar Guillaume Bernard de Sévérac bought a house near the church, where he established a monastery with 12 friars. A new, much larger church was built near or above the chapel of San Paolo in 1325. Thereafter the

voyage.name: Neve Shalom Synagogue
voyage.content: The most beautiful and the largest in the city where most of the religious ceremonies like bar-mitzvahs, weddings and funerals are held.

voyage.name: Ashkenazi Synagogue
voyage.content: The only active Ashkenazi Synagogue open to visits and prayers.

voyage.name: The Jewish Museum of Turkey
voyage.address: Bereketzade Mh, Büyük Hendek Cd 39, Beyoğlu
voyage.content: A former synagogue, the museum's exhibit details how the cultures mixed with and influenced each other in the past 500+ years since the Spanish expulsion.

voyage.name: Camondo Stairs
voyage.content: An attractive stairway mixing the Neo-Baroque and early Art Nouveau styles, climbing up from Bankalar St towards the Galata Tower. It was built in the 1870s by Abraham Salomon Camondo, who belonged to a prominent Ottoman-Venetian Jewish family of financiers and philanthropists.

voyage.name: Schneidertempel
voyage.content: This former synagogue of Ashkenazi Jews (many of German or French origin) now hosts an art gallery downstairs. Upstairs, there is an exhibition about the arrival and the lives of Ashkenazi Jews in Istanbul, with many original exhibits, including a letter from Albert Einstein. All explanations are in both Turkish and English.

voyage.name: Pera Museum
voyage.price: 20 TL, concession 10 TL, free on Fridays 18:00–22:00, students free on Wednesdays
voyage.content: A private museum with a large painting collection and archaeological collections of measurement units and tools used in Asia Minor since antiquity and faiences of Kütahya.

voyage.name: French Institute
voyage.alt: Institut français d'Istanbul / Fransız Kültür Merkezi
voyage.content: They have good art exhibits for free and sometimes have French films in the cinema.

voyage.name: Hagia Triada Greek Orthodox Church
voyage.content: A charming domed church built in 1880 at the side of Taksim Square, now uneasily contesting with Taksim Mosque for being the main landmark of the southern edge of the square.

voyage.name: S. Antonio di Padova Catholic Church
voyage.content: Although not at the size of Hagia Sophia, this is the largest active church in Turkey. It’s directly on Istiklal St, but somewhat hidden from view by its yard portal. Catholic Masses in Italian, Turkish, and English (in different days of the week).

voyage.name: Cezayir Street
voyage.content: Better known as Fransız Sokağı or La Rue Française, i.e. "French Street", is an alley of statues and geraniums hanging from windows, featuring France-themed restaurants, cafes, and pubs housed in renovated and brightly-painted neo-classical buildings. Upon its inauguration in its present form in 2005, there was a brief debate on how politically correct it would be to rename the street from Cezayir (Algeria) to Fransı

voyage.name: Museum of Innocence
voyage.price: 40 TL, 30 TL students, free admission on presentation of the novel
voyage.content: Opened in 2012, this museum is unique and a must-see when you are in the Beyoğlu area. It was created by Turkish Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk alongside a novel of the same name. It tells the love story of the two main characters from the novel, and represents life in Istanbul during the late 1970s to early 1980s, as it exhibits thousands of objects from that era.

voyage.name: Madame Tussauds
voyage.price: 650 TL; concessions when bought online and for domestic visitors
voyage.content: Wax museum with figures of Turkish and international celebrities.

voyage.name: İstanbul Modern
voyage.price: 350 TL, concessions for students and domestic visitors
voyage.content: A nice, organized museum with contemporary installations. It may be seen as overpriced given its small size. It also has a simple cafe.

voyage.name: Orhan Kemal Museum
voyage.content: Tiny house museum on the life of Turkish novelist Orhan Kemal (1914–1970).

voyage.name: Adam Mickiewicz Museum
voyage.content: A historic house museum dedicated to the life of Adam Mickiewicz, renowned Polish poet. This is where he lived while in Turkey from September 1855 to 26 November 1855, when he died of illness.

voyage.name: Miniaturk
voyage.content: It was built in 2001 and is the first miniature park in Istanbul (the world's largest miniature park in respect to its model area). The park hosts icons of many cultures and civilizations. Models vary from the Hagia Sophia to Galata Tower, from Safranbolu Houses to the Sumela Monastery in Trabzon, from Qubbat As-Sakhrah to the ruins of Mount Nemrut. In addition, some works that have not survived into the present, suc

voyage.name: Aynalıkavak Pavilion
voyage.price: 90 TL; concessions for students and domestic visitors
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00 (Closed Mon); you have to join the guided tours starting every 30 minutes in the high-season, and you may have all the place to yourself and the guide in winter
voyage.content: Started in 1613 by the Ottoman sultan Ahmet I (r. 1603–1617, who also had the Blue Mosque in the Old City built), and extensively renovated by the art-loving Selim III (r. 1789–1807), this sole building, which itself has the distinction of being the only intact structure that dates back to the rule of Ahmet III (r. 1703–1730), set inside a beautiful garden of pools and mature cedar and magnolia trees is the only rema

voyage.name: Rahmi M. Koç Industrial Museum
voyage.price: 600 TL (July 2024, about €17); concessions for students and domestic visitors
voyage.content: This is an industry museum showcasing the evolution of machines. Many transport related items including a submarine, classic cars, railway carriages, an out-of-service Bosphorus ferry and a Douglas DC-3 aircraft (possible to board) are on display, among others. Also houses a typical Istanbul streetscape with its shops and all as how it would look in the past.

voyage.name: Arter
voyage.content: A contemporary art museum.

voyage.name: Beyoglu Hagia Constantine Greek Orthodox Church
voyage.alt: Ayios Konstantinos ve Ayia Eleni Kilisesi
voyage.content: Greek Orthodox Church built in 1861.

voyage.name: Galataport
voyage.address: Kılıçali Paşa, Meclis-i Mebusan Cd. No:8
voyage.content: It includes the city's cruise ship terminal, around 250 shops, pubs and restaurants, a Peninsula hotel, the Istanbul Modern art museum, and other cultural and entertainment facilities; the complex also hosts festivals.

voyage.name: Haliçport
voyage.content: Also known as 'Tersane İstanbul'. Combines historic landmarks, blend of unique lifestyles and gastronomical delights, luxury homes and hotels, and a vibrant cultural calendar.

voyage.name: ArkeoPera
voyage.content: Best antiquarian bookshop in Turkey, owner knows every Turkish excavation site first hand.

voyage.name: Gonul Paksoy
voyage.content: Peerless one-of-a-kind dresses made for royalty from refined, antique Ottoman-era cloth.

voyage.name: Paristexas Concept Store
voyage.content: Sertaç Haznedaroğlu, the fashion-forward owner, stocks quirky Japanese labels and rare collections created for an Eastern market by designers such as Marc Jacobs, Vivienne Westwood and Chloé. Also check out custom-made leather bags and shoes by Turkish designer Ahmet Baytar.

voyage.name: Sedef Mum
voyage.content: Artisans of the time honoured art of candle making, intricately sculpted and aromatic wares make very portable gifts.

voyage.name: Bereket Döner
voyage.price: 13-23 TL for a full meal; can be substantially cheaper if you forgo salad or appetizers
voyage.content: A quite good value restaurant featuring döner (also on the plate as opposed to the usual wrap/sandwich variety; dipped in tomato sauce to the point of swimming) and traditional Turkish cuisine. The restaurant is a self-service one, i.e., you take a tray, and order your food by pointing at the entrance, and pay at the cash register right next to the food display (take your tableware and bread at this point as you won'

voyage.name: Şampiyon Kokoreç
voyage.content: A restaurant mostly focused in kokoreç — roasted and finely minced lamb intestines (yeap). It tastes great and is very budget-friendly: only 10 TL/wrap. Try stuffed mussels as well.

voyage.name: İbrahim Hakkı Uğrak Börek
voyage.content: A bit off the tourist track, the stone oven of this börek shop gives its products a distinctive flavour. Good value and friendly staff. Opens early, but not all varieties of börek will be ready first thing in the morning—the peynirli böreği is usually amongst the first out of the oven.

voyage.name: Degustasyon Restaurant
voyage.content: The restaurant is meyhane style, where lively conversation is the main dish on every table, next to fish and Rakı. A lot of negative reviews.

voyage.name: Ficcin
voyage.price: Around 20 TL per person without wine
voyage.content: The restaurant offers an exceptional value lunch, but is also pleasantly busy at night. Several of the staff speak English and foreign tourists are welcome alongside the many locals who eat there regularly. Fıccın is unusual in being a Circassian restaurant, which also serves Turkish food. Seats are available on the street and in several rooms inside. Alcohol is also served.

voyage.name: Nevizade Street
voyage.content: One of the most famous streets in Istiklal boulevard. It's narrow, and is mostly known for its meyhane style restaurants, where lively conversation is the main dish on every table, next to fish and Rakı that is.

voyage.name: Haci Abdullah Lokantası
voyage.address: Ağa Camii, Atıf Yılmaz Caddesi (Eski Sakizagaci Caddesi) No: 9/A
voyage.content: One of the best Ottoman restaurants in the country. You can find very traditional foods there. No alcohol.

voyage.name: Leb-i Derya
voyage.content: A nice cafe-restaurant with a splendid view of the Bosphorus and the Topkapi Palace in Tunel, Beyoglu.

voyage.name: The House Café
voyage.content: They serve giant salads, main dishes and pizzas pleasing even to the gourmets. The menu is seasonal which allows them to use only the freshest ingredients.

voyage.name: Miss Pizza Sishane
voyage.content: Very cozy Italian restaurant run by three women serving pizza, pasta, and salads.

voyage.name: Privato
voyage.price: Breakfast 65 TL per person, mains 30-40 TL
voyage.content: Traditional Turkish food with a focus on vegetarian dishes. Great for breakfast. Has a small patio in the back with a view of the Galata tower.

voyage.name: Zeytuna
voyage.content: Lebanese kitchen, from familiar, like falafel and hummus, to offbeat, like mutabal eggplant or mousaka chicken. Alcohol includes signature cocktails, named after Lebanon cities. There is a main hall and a bar, and the latter regularly hosts tango and salsa lessons, live blues, sometimes theatrical performances and film screenings.

voyage.name: 360 Istanbul
voyage.content: Great reviews for this rooftop restaurant with panoramic views.

voyage.name: Riddim Club Taksim
voyage.content: A complex with three floor. Rıddim live is the performance hall of complex and you can listen rock pop and alternative kinds of music. Riddim Special is the conceptual parties floor. İstanbul's best R&B-HipHop club is Rıddım R&B-HipHop (the 3rd floor).

voyage.name: Mektup Bar
voyage.content: Authentic live music. But, there is a restaurant, too. Do expect to pay a cover charge (approximately 15 TL) if there is a band playing.

voyage.name: Montreal Nevizade
voyage.content: Located in Nevizade where you can see so many small bars located next to each other, has live music and beer and shots in a subdued ambience of neon lights.

voyage.name: Snog Rooftop Bar
voyage.content: Good bar. But the attraction here is the stunning view.

voyage.name: Kadınlar Kahvesi
voyage.content: Different types of traditional Turkish coffees and snacks.

voyage.name: Hotel Mara
voyage.content: Central but tatty.

voyage.name: World House Hotel
voyage.content: Clean friendly hotel, no longer a hostel. No catering but there's a coffee shop below.

voyage.name: Midtown Hotel Istanbul
voyage.content: Smart business hotel.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu
voyage.content: Slick welcoming hotel.

voyage.name: Richmond Istanbul
voyage.content: Pleasant hotel in Beyoğlu district.

voyage.name: Misafir Suites
voyage.content: Huge chic modern rooms, but poor soundproofing for such a busy central spot.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Istanbul
voyage.content: Smart efficient hotel, the bar has stunning views in the evening. Mixed reviews for the restaurants.

voyage.name: Pera Palace
voyage.content: Opened in 1892 and sitting on a hill overlooking the Golden Horn. They make much of their history, and a stellar cast of celebs have stayed here, including Agatha Christie. They claim she wrote Murder on the Orient Express in room 411, though she probably wrote the first draft in Arpachiyah in Iraq. Atatürk often used Room 101 in the early days of the Republic, and that's now a museum.

voyage.name: Marmara Taksim
voyage.content: Occasion lapses, but mostly glowing reviews for this upscale hotel with great views over the Bosphorus.

voyage.name: Witt Istanbul Hotel
voyage.content: Modern hotel with 17 suites in Scandi style. It's up a steep hill from the tram stop.

voyage.name: Tomtom Suites
voyage.address: Tomtom Kaptan Sk 18, off Boğazkesen Cd
voyage.content: Wonderful hotel with spacious luxury suites in the 1850s home of the Soeurs Gardes Malades, a Franciscan order. Tomtom was a captain in the Ottoman navy.

voyage.name: Dolmabahce Palace
voyage.price: Foreigners pay 1200 TL for Selamlık + Harem + Painting Museum, Domestic Visitors 170 TL, Müzeumkart not accepted
voyage.content: This lavish palace with 285 rooms and 43 halls was the admin centre for the Ottoman Empire in its last 60 years. The palace government block (Selamlık) includes the Imperial Mabeyn (State Apartments) and Muayede Hall (Ceremonial Hall), while the Imperial Harem was the sultan's private quarters. Also here are the Painting Gallery, Music Museum, Clock Museum and Museum of Palace Collections. Free audio guide in several

voyage.name: Akaretler Street
voyage.content: Akaretler Caddesi, or officially Süleyman Seba Caddesi features upscale garment boutiques, restaurants, and sidewalk cafés housed in renovated late Ottoman-era rowhouses built for the state elite, given their proximity to Dolmabahçe Palace, imperial headquarters then.

voyage.name: Linden Palace
voyage.content: A 19th-century neo-Baroque manor built as an imperial summer retreat in a valley, named after the linden grove in its grounds.

voyage.name: Yıldız Palace
voyage.hours: 08:00–19:00 during summer, and till 17:00 during winter
voyage.content: A vast complex of former imperial Ottoman pavilions and villas in Istanbul, Turkey, built in the 19th and early 20th centuries. It was used as a residence by the Sultan and his court in the late 19th century.

voyage.name: Ortaköy
voyage.content: A neighbourhood on the bank of Bosphorus with the Ortaköy Mosque—the baroque mosque under the Bosphorus Bridge, combination of which are one of the most iconic images of Istanbul. This artsy neighbourhood is filled with nice cafes, some of which offer kumpir—a baked potato with various fillings such as mayonnaise, ketchup, pickles, sweetcorn, sausage slices, carrots, mushrooms, Russian salad among others&

voyage.name: Arnavutköy
voyage.content: The neighbourhood of Arnavutköy (literally "Albanian village", paying homage to its founders in the 16th century) features impressive yalıs, multiple-storey wooden mansions lining the waterfront, and all bearing significant artwork on their facades. Beware there are two areas called Arnavutköy - the other is the site of the new airport, away northwest of the city.

voyage.name: Rumeli Fortress
voyage.content: Built in first half of the 15th century, this is the large medieval castle under the Second Bosphorus Bridge. Its former name Boğazkesen (Turkish)/Laimokopia (Greek) means both "strait-blocker" and "throat-cutter" in both languages and denotes the reason of its building—to shut the supply routes from the Black Sea in the north into the slowly falling apart Byzantine Empire through the Bosphorus. Rumeli, literal

voyage.name: Baltalimanı Japanese Garden
voyage.content: Built with support of Shimonoseki, one of Istanbul's sister cities, the garden features a tea room, ponds, waterfalls, as well as a cherry lane.

voyage.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
voyage.hours: Tue Thu Fri Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed Sat 10:00-22:00
voyage.content: Museum with a rich collection of calligraphy and paintings. It also hosts temporary exhibitions of works by some world-class artists such as Pablo Picasso from time to time.

voyage.name: Ural Ataman Classic Car Museum
voyage.address: Ferahevler, Nuri Paşa Cd. No:107, Sarıyer

voyage.name: Emirgan Park
voyage.content: Situated on the gentle hill overlooking the neighbourhood of Emirgan and the Bosphorus, Emirgan Park was for long the only place in the city where Istanbulites can admire the beauty of tulips. Having lost that distinction since the first decade of the 2000s as tulips are now everywhere, this is still a beautiful park with artificial ponds, small waterfalls, and impressive views of the Bosphorus. There are also cafes

voyage.name: Sadberk Hanım Museum
voyage.content: A private museum housed in a yalı, the traditional wooden waterfront mansions that line the banks of the Bosphorus. The exhibition includes a number of archaeological and ethnographical artifacts from the collection of the long-time entrepreneur and industrialist Koç Family, though just seeing the interior of a yalı is worth entering.

voyage.name: Yusuf Ziya Mansion
voyage.address: Rumeli Hisarı, Balta Limanı Hisar Cd. No:5, Sarıyer
voyage.content: It houses the headquarters of Borusan Holding and the Borusan Contemporary art museum. The popular nickname of the mansion, Perili Köşk (meaning the "Haunted Mansion") refers to its construction remaining partially unfinished for a long period (its second and third floors remained empty for decades.)

voyage.name: Belgrad Forest
voyage.content: Named after a 16th-century village, founded by Serbs deported from Belgrade when it fell to the Ottomans. The village was popular as a forest resort, but its inhabitants were resettled in the 19th century and it's now a bosky ruin. The forest is mostly primordial and deciduous, predominantly oak. It's dotted with ancient aqueducts and dams as this area was a water catchment for Constantinople / Istanbul, and has lots

voyage.name: Atatürk Arboretum
voyage.price: Adult weekend 60 TL, weekdays 30 TL, card payment only
voyage.content: From Bahçeköy village, follow the road into Belgrad Forest towards Kemerburgaz for 10 mins. The arboretum, surrounded by a natural oak forest, is planted with many non-native tree species (many turning crimson/golden/purple as winter approaches) and has a pond with feisty ducks. It's an almost mystic place during hazy autumn days, but is always very scenic no matter what the season. Watch for migratory birds in autum

voyage.name: Beşiktaş Stadium
voyage.content: Homecourt of Beşiktaş JK

voyage.name: Sarıyer Bird Observatory Tower.
voyage.address: Garipçe, Sarıyer Rumeli Feneri Yolu No:4359, Sarıyer
voyage.content: Nr 1 place in the city for birdwatching.

voyage.name: Akmerkez
voyage.content: At Etiler. Nearest metro station is Gayrettepe/Zincirlikuyu. The mall is about 25-min walk or 10-min taxi ride away from that station.

voyage.name: İstinye Park
voyage.content: Beautiful upscale mall with 300 stores, many good restaurants and cafes.

voyage.name: Iznik Foundation
voyage.content: Offers neo-Iznik pottery after recreating original formulas from original Iznik kilns, which functioned between 1450 and 1650.

voyage.name: Beşiktaş Market
voyage.content: This is where locals go shopping. If you are keen to buy fruits, vegetables, walnuts or olives at local prices, this is where you should head. It is always a good idea to bring rome walnuts or olives back home. Otherwise it is just nice to visit and soak in the atmosphere. This is an authentic market not to be missed.

voyage.name: Yeşil Çiftlik Restaurant
voyage.address: Kilyos Yolu Uskumruköy Kavsağı No:30 Sariyer/Istanbul
voyage.content: Special lamb barbecue, kebabs, country breakfast, beer, rakı and other alcoholic drinks, Nargile (Waterpipe, Sheesha) available.

voyage.name: Vagabondo's Ristorante & Pizzeria
voyage.address: Köybaşı Cad. Yalılar Durağı No: 168 Yeniköy / İstanbul
voyage.content: Italian cuisine; pizza, steak, pasta, wines and other alcohol available.

voyage.name: Güzelyer Yedigün Balık Lokantasi
voyage.address: Rumelikavagi karakutuk cad. No: 96 Tellibaba ustu, 34450 Sarıyer
voyage.content: Great seafood restaurant at the cost.

voyage.name: Uzunya Beach Restaurant
voyage.content: Cozy seafood restaurant at the Black Sea. Very popular for weekend breakfasts.

voyage.name: Sans
voyage.content: Nice restaurant in a small garden serving Turkish and Mediterranean food.

voyage.name: Park Fora
voyage.address: Muallim Naci Caddesi, Cemil Topuzlu Parkı
voyage.content: Great seafood, located in Kuruçeşme park right on the edge of the sea, it has a very nice view of the Bosphorus and Bosphorus Bridge. The waiters know English.

voyage.name: Divan Brasserie Bebek
voyage.address: Bebek, Cevdet Paşa Cd. No: 28/A, 34342 Beşiktaş
voyage.content: At first sight it may seem like a mere patisserie, but walk downstairs and you will find a lovely restaurant with the waters of the Bosporus right next to you. The food is simply first-class and the service is very good, too.

voyage.name: Ulus 29
voyage.content: Upscale restaurant with an amazing view over the Bosporus.

voyage.name: Kazan
voyage.content: A quite elegantly decorated local pub in which fans of Beşiktaş FC that could not make it to the stadium, old and young, male and female, like to watch the games on live broadcast. During summer months, they also have an open-air section just next to the sidewalk where smoking is free. Quite good value and is actually cheaper than how it looks in the first glance.

voyage.name: Ciragan Palace Kempinski
voyage.content: This hotel is in a residence of the last Sultan. Rooms come with air-con, TV, minibar and safety deposit box. Hotel has several restaurants and lounges, pools, jacuzzi, Turkish baths, gym and other amenities.

voyage.name: W Istanbul
voyage.content: WiFi, Fitness center and business center onsite as well as a fine dining restaurant.

voyage.name: Swissôtel The Bosphorus
voyage.content: A 5-star hotel near Taksim Square with four restaurants and two bars.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Bosphorus Hotel, Istanbul
voyage.content: 120 rooms and 7 meeting rooms with technical equipment, wellness center, and underground parking. The hotel has one all day dining restaurant, one bar and a private venue that highlight the city as Starboard Restaurant offers a spectacular Bosphorus view; "Cruise Lounge & Bar", with its scenery; and "Pupa Terrace", a venue for private events, dinners, or cocktails.

voyage.name: Eyüp Mosque Complex
voyage.content: This is the main attraction around this part of the city. The holiest Islamic shrine in the city, the complex includes, right next to the mosque, the tomb of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (Eyüp Ensari Türbesi), the standard bearer of Prophet Mohammad, died and buried here during the first Muslim siege of Constantinople (674-678 AD). The neighbourhood was named after him. Muslims flock here (in such huge numbers that sometimes

voyage.name: Artistanbul Feshane
voyage.content: Feshane began as a factory producing fezzes (fes), the red hats made of felt adopted by the Ottomans in the early 19th century as a part of westernizing efforts in lieu of much more traditional turbans. However, the fez was scrapped in favour of western garments during Atatürk's reforms of the 1920s and 30s as it was thought to symbolize the old, decidedly oriental regime. A restoration in 1998 made it a cultural and

voyage.name: Santral İstanbul
voyage.address: Silahtar Mh Kazım Karabekir Cd 1, Eyüp
voyage.content: A contemporary art museum in a building converted from an old power plant: 1914-built and coal-fired, this was the oldest in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire. Part of the plant was kept in almost exact original condition and now serves as the "Energy Museum".

voyage.name: Cable car
voyage.price: The same price as in public transport, 2.6TL for IstanbulCard holders and 5TL for others
voyage.content: Offers a very short ride (3 min) up the nearby hill. And it can get very crowded during summer.

voyage.name: Vialand
voyage.price: US$55, under 3 free, discount for domestic visitors
voyage.content: The only theme park of the city has a good selection of rides, including a couple of rollercoasters.

voyage.name: Rami Library
voyage.address: Yeni Rami Mahallesi, Rami Kışla Cd. 98/1 Eyüpsultan
voyage.content: 19th century barracks serving as municipality library.

voyage.name: Akmanoğlu Fırını
voyage.content: This is the bakery where halkas mentioned in the "See" section, as well as a number of other traditional cookies, both sweet and salty, are produced and sold.

voyage.name: Lale Lokantasi
voyage.content: Traditional Turkish/Ottoman cuisine.

voyage.name: La Mekan
voyage.address: Emniyettepe, Mareşal Fevzi Çakmak Cd. No:60 D:1
voyage.content: Also a grill restaurant next door, Çınaraltı.

voyage.name: Pierre Loti
voyage.content: An open air café on a hill overlooking the Golden Horn in Eyüp. It’s rumored that the French writer the place is named after used to love visiting this café during his residence in Istanbul. The cable car up here offers some nice views. It’s also possible to walk uphill or to take a taxi.

voyage.name: Turquhouse Boutique Hotel
voyage.address: Merkez Mah. İdris Köşkü Caddesi, Eyüp
voyage.content: A boutique hotel housed in 7 separate buildings in the same yard. Rooms with en-suite bathrooms, air-con, satellite TV, and wireless internet access.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Istanbul Golden Horn Turkey
voyage.content: Near the banks of the Horn.

voyage.name: Atatürk Museum
voyage.content: A historic 3-storey house, easily distinguishable among the modern apartment buildings thanks to its brightly coloured and gracefully decorated exterior. This is where the future founder of the Turkish Republic, Kemal Atatürk rented in 1919 while staying in Istanbul before setting sail to Samsun on the Black Sea coast to start the Turkish War of Independence. Hosts Atatürk-related paraphernalia and photos.

voyage.name: Military Museum
voyage.content: Among the exhibition of this museum are five thousand pieces from the Ottoman era through WWII, with the most prominent piece possibly being the huge chain that the Byzantines stretched across the mouth of the Golden Horn to keep out the Sultan's navy in 1453 during the siege of Constantinople. In the yard of the museum, the Janissary Band (Mehter Takımı), the world’s oldest military band gives concerts of march musi

voyage.name: Radio Building
voyage.content: This building dating back to 1945 houses the local radio branch of the state radio and television corporation of Turkey (TRT). Not exactly an architectural pearl (although fans of the 1940s' totalitarian architecture will likely find its stately façade interesting), but it is prominent for the part it played in the political history of Turkey: It was occupied three times by the Army, in 1960, 1971, and most recently

voyage.name: Nişantaşı
voyage.content: A neighbourhood east of Şişli known for its Art Nouveau apartment buildings, the ground floors of many of which are upmarket restaurants, cafes, pubs, and garment stores lining the sidewalks. Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk, well-known Turkish novelist, is a lifelong resident of the neighbourhood which formed the background of several of his novels.

voyage.name: HISART Museum
voyage.address: Hürriyet, Dr. Cemil Bengü Cd. No:21

voyage.name: WW1 Monument
voyage.content: Next to the Court of Istanbul.

voyage.name: Attend the Tataula Carnival
voyage.content: Despite a 1943 ban on this Greek Orthodox pre-Lent carnival by the Turkish authorities, it has been revived since 2010. The tradition began in the 19th century or earlier, and even though the event was led by local Greeks, the celebrations were open to everyone. It's also a nice opportunity to look into Turkey's multicultural past. Takes place in the Kurtuluş (previously named Tataula) neighborhood.

voyage.name: Maçka Park
voyage.content: This park occupies the sides of a valley of this "city of seven hills", with an avenue in the bottom. A 4-person gondola lift line is strung over it, offering a shortcut when walking between Beşiktaş and Taksim Square as well as nice views of the Bosphorus (access to the northern station from Maçka Cd and Eytam Cd, every 5 minutes 08:00-20:00, 1.50 TL pp one-way). There is also a wooden bridge over the bisecting aven

voyage.name: Ali Sami Yen Complex
voyage.content: Homecourt of Galatasaray SK

voyage.name: Cevahir
voyage.content: The newest one of malls in Istanbul. At Şişli. Metro: Şişli-Mecidiyeköy. Also accessible from Mecidiyeköy Metrobus Station.

voyage.name: Profilo
voyage.content: Located a bit away from main street (about 10 min walk) at Mecidiyeköy. Metro: Şişli-Mecidiyeköy. Also accessible from Mecidiyeköy Metrobus Station.

voyage.name: Metrocity
voyage.content: Levent metro station has a direct exit to the mall.

voyage.name: Kanyon
voyage.content: one of the most exclusive shopping malls in Istanbul with sophisticated, modernistic architecture, has a connection to Levent subway station and to Metrocity by an underground passage.

voyage.name: Sultana's Dinner and 1001 Nights Show
voyage.content: In Elmadag, near Taksim, has traditional Turkish cuisine (meze, kebabs, desserts) with a show every evening of belly dancing, Turkish folklore and live music.

voyage.name: Set Kebap
voyage.content: Has a wonderful meze table and delicious Adana Kebab. The staff speaks very little English but are most anxious to be helpful.

voyage.name: Kosebasi Kebap
voyage.content: This Zagat-rated kebab joint serves traditional Turkish kebabs in modern/ upscale atmosphere. Levent is the main branch but they have 7 more locations (including 3 express versions) in Istanbul.

voyage.name: Sosa
voyage.content: Fairly priced salads and wraps among others.

voyage.name: Kristal Ocakbaşı
voyage.content: Classic Turkish steak-house.

voyage.name: Maslak
voyage.content: A neighborhood with dozens of luxury eateries, both in local and international fashion.

voyage.name: Levent
voyage.content: A neighborhood which is just across the Sapphire of Istanbul and hosts nice bars.

voyage.name: Taps
voyage.content: A bar, restaurant and brewery in one. The crowd is the general Nişantaşı crowd, it also attracts a lot of expatriates.

voyage.name: Istanbul Suites
voyage.address: Ergenekon Mh, Harbiye Çayırı Sk 111, Şişli
voyage.content: Ranging from duplex to studio apartments which are all furnished with modern appliances. It's located in the city center and is within a 5 minute walking distance to Taksim. Possibility for short and long term rentals.

voyage.name: Gallery Residence Hotel
voyage.address: Vali Konağı Cd, Süleyman Nazik Sk 10, Nişantaşı
voyage.content: Suites with fully equipped kitchens, DVD players, and fax machines. Free wi-fi, breakfast, sauna, jacuzzi, and fitness.

voyage.name: Jazz Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star jazz-themed hotel with 12 rooms named after famous jazz artists. Free wi-fi and breakfast.

voyage.name: Arts Hotel
voyage.content: Modern and elegant hotel.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Istanbul
voyage.content: 5-star with 360 rooms and suites overlooking the city and the Bosphorus. Hotel has formal dining, outdoor pool, Turkish bath, fitness center and business center.

voyage.name: Hilton Istanbul Bosphorus
voyage.content: Family-friendly hotel offers a business center, child-friendly restaurants, fitness facilities with massage parlour, pool and Turkish baths. Rooms have private balconies with views of the Bosphorus and high speed internet access. Opened to service in 1955, this has the distinction of being the oldest Hilton outside the US.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Istanbul - Maçka Palas
voyage.content: 5-star hotel in the residential and shopping district of Nisantasi. Rooms have wi-fi and combine Art Deco style and historic Turkish decor. The hotel also has a spa, swimming pool and restaurants.

voyage.name: Ritz-Carlton
voyage.content: Standing tall near the Bosphorus, this 5-star hotel overlooks the Bosphorus and Dolmabahce Palace.

voyage.name: Çatalca
voyage.content: A small town 40 km west of central Istanbul and 15 km north of Büyükçekmece that had a substantial Greek population until the 1920s transfers. Spared from destruction in the Balkan wars which foreshadowed the Great War, the old quarter has many historic wooden buildings and fountains in leafy squares. A short stretch of the old town walls still stand just north of the centre. In the outer areas, bunkers of the WW2 'Ç

voyage.name: Population Transfer Museum
voyage.content: The town's main sight, housed in a red brick neoclassical building erected as a Greek tavern, this museum commemorates the forced population transfer of 1922–26, whereby Greeks living in Turkey were expelled to Greece, while the Turks of Greece were expelled to Turkey.

voyage.name: Cave Monastery of İnceğiz
voyage.content: A Byzantine monastery complex carved into a cliff, set in a lush valley. The site is free, but May-Sept there's a 32 TL toll for cars on the access roads. There's a picnic area, pity about all the trash, and a couple of restaurants nearby.

voyage.name: Kurşunlugerme
voyage.content: A remarkable Roman double aqueduct above the village of Gümüşpınar. Here water from two catchments converged then flowed by an upper and lower channel all the way to Constantinople. In 2020 treasure hunters got it into their heads that gold was buried beneath, so they blew it up, incurring substantial damage..

voyage.name: Anastasian Wall
voyage.content: it was a defensive wall built in the 5th century to protect Constantinople from barbarian attack from the west. It ran for 56 km from Evcik on the Black Sea coast right across the Thracian peninsula to Silivri on the Marmara coast. Unlike the better-known Hadrian's Wall in England, it was neither well-constructed nor well-garrisoned, so the barbarians gleefully overran it, and it was abandoned in the 7th century. Muc

voyage.name: Evcik Beach
voyage.content: A wide, undeveloped sandy beach backed by cliffs, unexpectedly popular during summer weekends despite its relative remoteness. A narrow track steeply descends to it, but it's best to park your car ahead of the slope to avoid climbing back up in reverse. The ruins of the Byzantine church of St George over the bluff mark the northern end of the Anastasian Wall.

voyage.name: Yalıköy
voyage.content: The most interesting of the resorts along this part of the coast. The beach has multi-coloured stones much used as garden mosaics in the city. (Modern quarries nearby still extract these for the Turkish glass industry.) The town has restaurants and accommodation.

voyage.name: Binkılıç
voyage.content: A village which has accommodation and old wooden houses. Past Binkılıç, the highway eventually reaches Saray in the neighbouring province of Tekirdağ.

voyage.name: Çilingoz Nature Park
voyage.price: 155 TL/car daily use, 195 TL/car night stays
voyage.content: It has a sandy beach backed by forest where a creek runs out. This is as far as you can go in a standard car.

voyage.name: Pirate Cove
voyage.content: A small and very isolated beach surrounded by rock cliffs.

voyage.name: Kastro
voyage.content: A relatively developed beach.

voyage.name: Silivri
voyage.content: A resort on the Marmara coast. It's the westernmost part of Istanbul, between Çatalca and the province of Tekirdağ. There are some remnants of the Anastasian wall here, the scrappy ruins of a castle, an ancient cistern, the Piri Paşa Mosque, and Uzunköprü the long aqueduct.

voyage.name: Germiyan Church
voyage.content: An early 19th century church built for the local Greek Orthodox 5 km north of Değirmenköy. After they left the area in the 1920s, it served as the village schoolhouse until a landslide in the 1960s forced the relocation of the village to its current location south. Since then, it stands derelict and lonely on an atmospheric hillside, together with the ruins of a 1940s mosque about 100 m to its south — the only remain

voyage.name: Between Two Seas
voyage.content: A 60-km, 4-day hiking trail between the coasts of the Marmara and Black Seas across the rapidly changing outskirts of the city, passing through various urban, natural, historic, and industrial sites.

voyage.name: The Sultan's Trail
voyage.content: A 2,500-km hiking and cycling trail stretching all the way to Vienna, retracing the campaign of Suleiman the Magnificent onto the Habsburg capital. It is not marked on the ground, but the GPS tracks are available through its website. In the east, it kicks off at the mausoleum of Suleiman in Istanbul's Old City, while to the west the next major town is Saray.

voyage.name: Avlu34
voyage.address: Arnavutköy Merkez, 23 Nisan Cd. No 1, Arnavutköy
voyage.content: A shopping center.

voyage.name: Kemerburgaz
voyage.content: A village (and nowadays a commuter suburb) at the edge of the forest, 15 km north of Eyüp and 10 km west of Bahçeköy. Several ancient aqueducts stand nearby, notably Kurt Kemeri ("Wolf's Aqueduct") and Uzun Kemer ("Long Aqueduct"). The oldest were Byzantine, but rebuilt, and others added, in the 16th century to boost the water supply to the city. The residents were Greek until the 1920s population exchange, when Turk

voyage.name: Göktürk
voyage.content: A upscale neighborhood with various cafes, pubs and restaurants scattered.

voyage.name: Silivri Marina
voyage.content: There are cafes, pubs and restaurants along the pier.

voyage.name: Ramada Plaza by Wyndham Silivri
voyage.address: Çanta Sancaktepe, Hacı Nurettin Akbulut Cd. No13, Silivri

voyage.name: Hampton by Hilton
voyage.address: Mehmet Akif Ersoy, Görele Sk No 1, Arnavutköy

voyage.name: Maiden's Tower
voyage.content: One of the icons of the city is also called the Leander's Tower, on a Bosphorus islet off Salacak. The local myth ascribes its name to a princess, whose father wanted to protect her in this offshore tower from a prophecy that she would be killed by a snakebite on her birthday, but the snake found its way inside a basket of fruits — ironically a birthday present from her father — and you've probably already guessed th

voyage.name: Selimiye Barracks
voyage.content: Also Florence Nightingale Museum.

voyage.name: Kuzguncuk
voyage.content: This attractive neighbourhood was home to a large Christian and Jewish population until some decades ago and still has a number of sights like two synagogues, some churches among which the Armenian Surp Krikor Lusavoriç, dozens of wooden houses and a Jewish and Christian cemetery.

voyage.name: Beylerbeyi
voyage.content: is a small port with a popular fishing dock. There are many restaurants: those on the port-side serve alcohol and are moderately expensive, those down the side-streets are cheaper. Notable buildings include the 18th-century Hamid-i Evvel mosque, and the 19th-century highway tunnel (which is closed as of Dec 2018). But the standout attraction is the palace.

voyage.name: Beylerbeyi Palace
voyage.content: Bling palace-cum-summer house in mid-19th-century Ottoman style. Notable for its reception hall, bathing pavilion, and second floor restroom with spectacular Bosphorus view. Visit by guided tour only, these start every half-hour.

voyage.name: Çengelköy
voyage.content: About 15 minutes walking north of Beylerbeyi lies the historical fishing village Çengelköy. Its long history is attested by an 800-year-old sycamore tree on one of the two main terraced squares, and the Byzantine Aya Yorgi church. The restaurants and piers of Çengelköy offer some of the best panoramas along the Bosphorus, including a view on the old city under the first bridge. The neighborhood was popular amongst TV

voyage.name: Kuleli Military Academy
voyage.content: One of the oldest functioning academies.

voyage.name: Çamlıca Hill
voyage.content: One of the highest hills of Istanbul, at 288 m asl. Since it dominates a great part of the city, it is the site of Çamlıca Tower, a 2021-built telecommunications tower and the highest structure of Istanbul, with observation decks (daily 10:00-22:00, 450 TL, discount for domestic visitors). The rest of the summit is a public park dotted by cafes with an Ottoman-themed decor. The park is sponsored by the government, so

voyage.name: Anadolu Citadel
voyage.content: A medieval citadel on the Bosphorus at the mouth of the Göksu creek. It was built in the late 14th century to control (polite word for "choke off") shipping along the Bosphorus, which narrows to 660 m at this point. It worked in tandem with Rumeli Citadel, built some 50 years later on the European bank. It fell into disrepair but was restored in the 1990s. You can't go in, but it's a pleasant setting; the entire vill

voyage.name: Küçüksu Palace
voyage.content: If you are already in the area, it's worth considering to visit this waterside neo-Baroque manor, built in the 19th century for the countryside and hunting excursions of the Ottoman dynasty. The area, where the Göksu River flows into the Bosphorus, was known as "the Sweet Waters of Asia" by the pioneer European travellers of the epoch (as opposed to "the Sweet Waters of Europe", another contemporary elite recreationa

voyage.name: Anadolu Kavağı
voyage.content: A village with an impressive citadel overlooking the Bosphorus and its mouth into the Black Sea. By land it's accessible only by a hairpinning road through the forest, with few buses. It's best reached by ferry from Eminönü (twice daily) or Sariyer (frequent). In the village, a road is signposted up to the hilltop Yoros citadel (a little more than 1 km, 20 min on foot, free admission). There's a pleasant area with ca

voyage.name: Yoros Castle
voyage.content: It's as close as the casual visitor to Istanbul gets to the Black Sea. Not much of a vista but it allows you to appreciate the strategic significance of the Bosphorus.

voyage.name: Polonezköy
voyage.content: The "Polish village" was founded in 1842 by Polish settlers in the wake of the failed uprising against Russian Imperial rule, and reinforced by more settlers after every subsequent civil upheaval until Poland's independence in 1918. Most then returned, but several stayed on, adopting Turkish citizenship but maintaining their Polish language and culture. The village has houses in traditional Polish style, a 1914 littl

voyage.name: Emaar Square
voyage.content: Complex with a shopping centre, a skydeck and an aquarium.

voyage.name: Tarihi Çinili Hamamı
voyage.content: Turkish bath cheaper than the more touristy ones in the European side.

voyage.name: Üsküdar Musical Society
voyage.address: Halk Cd Emin Ongan Sk 10, Üsküdar
voyage.content: Founded in 1918, the society is often considered the most respected of the social clubs offering classes in the classical Ottoman music, and catching up with their frequent public concerts is certainly a good way of entering the vast world of this genre.

voyage.name: Nakkaştepe
voyage.content: A park right next to the Bosphorus Bridge. Comes with an unforgettable zipline experience.

voyage.name: Validebağ Park
voyage.content: Also Sultan Abdülaziz Hunting Lodge and Hababam Museum.

voyage.name: Joshua's Hill
voyage.content: Believed to be the tomb of the biblical Joshua, it's the steepest hill in Istanbul which is closest to the sea.

voyage.name: Black Sea Coast
voyage.content: There's a string of small coastal resorts, from Poyrazköy just beyond the north Bosphorus bridge, through Anadolufenerli, Riva. Usual beach attractions, but the Black Sea is often rough so beware of the waves. There is also a big golf field, 'Mustafa V. Koç Course'.

voyage.name: Kanaat Lokantası
voyage.content: Kanaat Lokantası, which dates back to 1933, is famous for its traditional Ottoman cuisine as well as a variety of fascinating desserts. The prices are reasonable but they accept nothing but cash.

voyage.name: İmren Restaurant
voyage.address: Validei Atik mah, Miroğlu Sk. 10/A, 34664 Üsküdar
voyage.content: Serves traditional Turkish food. You could try kelle paca soup or doner here.

voyage.name: Nakkaş Kebap
voyage.address: Gümüşyolu Cad. Eski Taş Ocağı Sokak No:27, Nakkaştepe
voyage.content: A large restaurant with traditional Turkish kebap and "mezes" (appetizers).

voyage.name: Ajia Hotel
voyage.address: Çubuklu Cad. Ahmet Rasim Paşa Yalısı No:27, 34810 Beykoz
voyage.content: Boutique waterfront hotel. Rooms include air-con, TV, safe, Wi-Fi.
